You are extending a YouTube video editing pipeline (Windows, ffmpeg-based). Main script:

C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\first-video\edit\scripts\composite_full.py

Read it in full first — read the CURRENT file on disk, it has been modified multiple times by other agents this session, don't rely on any assumed prior state.

## The bug

The neon-glow border loop (`NEON_BORDER` = `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\first-video\edit\animations\slot_neon_border_loop\render.webm`, 1920x1080 60fps VP9-alpha, 14.4s seamless loop, recently redesigned to be a thin crisp line hugging a 576x432 box with r=28 corner radius at ZERO gap — read its own `index.html` source for the exact geometry if useful) is currently only composited around the webcam in `build_webcam_primary()` (the full-screen "hero stage" layout). `build_screen_primary()` (the screen-recording + webcam-PIP layout, used for most of the video) still uses the OLDER plain treatment — `pip_mask.png` (rounded corner mask), `pip_shadow.png` (drop shadow), `pip_ring.png` (subtle glass edge highlight) — with NO neon border at all. The user wants the neon border present on the webcam PIP at ALL times, including throughout `screen_primary` segments, not just in the full-webcam hero shots.

## What you need to handle correctly

`build_screen_primary()`'s webcam PIP is exactly 576x432 (`PIP_W`/`PIP_H`) — which is exactly the box the neon border asset was authored for (r=28, zero gap, centered on the 1920x1080 canvas by default). So for the STATIC case this should be simple: composite the border (no rescaling needed — `NEON_SCALE` factor of 1.0) at the same x/y position as the PIP itself.

But `build_screen_primary()`'s PIP position is NOT always static within a segment — read the function carefully:
- `pos_key` can be `"bottom_right"` or `"bottom_left"` (see `POS` dict) and DIFFERENT segments can use different corners (`POSITION_OVERRIDES`).
- When `prev_pos_key != pos_key` (the position changed from the previous segment), the PIP SLIDES from the old x to the new x over `SLIDE_DUR` (0.6s), via a `t`-varying `x_expr` (an eased cubic slide, already implemented — see the `ease`/`x_expr`/`shx_expr`/`shx` logic). The border needs to track this slide in lockstep — same x-position expression, same timing — so it visually stays attached to the PIP through the slide, not lagging or static while the PIP moves.
- There's also `ZOOMS` — a Ken-Burns zoom applied to the SCREEN RECORDING background in some segments — but this does NOT affect the webcam PIP or its size/position at all (confirm this by reading `zoom_filter()`'s usage — it's only applied to `[0:v]` the screen input, not the webcam). So the border does NOT need to account for zoom, only for the existing PIP slide-position logic.

Read the project's established gotchas before writing filter expressions: `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\tools\video-use\helpers\zoom_filter.py`'s docstring (eval=frame requirements for scale/pad, `overlay`'s x/y DOES support `t`-varying expressions while `pad`'s x/y does NOT, parenthesization of `round()` expressions, alpha-webm needs explicit `-c:v libvpx-vp9` on decode). Also worth reading how `build_webcam_primary()` already handles the border (both its static hero-scale case and, if present, whatever continuous-scale-during-transition technique was used for the dynamic shrink-aside case — there's likely a working reference pattern in there for compositing a frame-varying-positioned border via `overlay` that you can adapt, rather than inventing the technique from scratch).

## Implementation

Add the neon border as a new layer in `build_screen_primary()`'s filter chain, positioned/timed to exactly match the webcam PIP's existing `x_expr`/`py` (or the slide-eased equivalent) at every frame — same z-order convention as the rest of the file (border behind the webcam content, i.e. composited before the webcam overlay step, same layering principle used elsewhere: shadow/ring/border sit behind, webcam video itself is drawn on top last so it's never occluded). Decide whether to keep `pip_ring.png` (the subtle glass edge highlight) alongside the new neon border, or whether the neon border now makes it redundant — your call, but check visually which reads better (the neon border is a much stronger visual element; the ring was designed as a subtle highlight for the OLD non-neon look, it may look redundant or muddy stacked with the neon border — inspect a rendered frame and decide, don't just leave both blindly). Keep `pip_shadow.png` (the drop shadow) unless you find a visual reason not to — the neon border and the drop shadow serve different purposes (glow vs. depth) and likely both still make sense together, but verify.

## Verification (mandatory — read carefully)

This exact codebase has shipped "verified" work that turned out broken multiple times this session, always because verification only checked a couple of convenient timestamps. For this task:
- Rebuild a handful of representative `screen_primary` segments, INCLUDING at least one where `POSITION_OVERRIDES` causes a corner change from the previous segment (so you exercise the slide-tracking logic) — e.g. segments around index 26-28 (the prompt-typing beat switches to `bottom_left`) are a good candidate; confirm the actual current indices/positions yourself from `POSITION_OVERRIDES` in the file, don't assume.
- Extract frames at multiple points within a slide transition (not just before/after) to confirm the border visually tracks the PIP's position with no lag, no mismatch, no popping — the border's left/right/top/bottom edges should align with the webcam content's edges at every sampled frame, including mid-slide.
- Extract frames from a segment with NO position change (static PIP) to confirm the simple case still looks right (border present, correctly positioned, no regression to the shadow/mask/ring).
- Confirm alpha-correctness the established way if you touch anything alpha-related: explicit `-c:v libvpx-vp9` on decode, real pixel sampling, not just ffprobe metadata.
- Rebuild `composited_draft.mp4` via `main()` afterward (this will need to rebuild every `screen_primary` segment since they all gain the new border — that's expected, let the script's existing caching/rebuild logic handle it) and confirm it decodes cleanly end-to-end (`ffmpeg -v error -i composited_draft.mp4 -f null -`).

## Deliverable

Modified `composite_full.py`, rebuilt `composited_draft.mp4`, and a written report: the technique used to track the border to the PIP's position (including through the slide), what you decided about `pip_ring.png` and why, and your verification results (actual frames checked, what you saw, including at least one mid-slide frame). Do not ask clarifying questions — investigate and make the most reasonable, well-verified call on anything ambiguous, and document the decision.

377	def build_transition(seg_a: Path, seg_b: Path, out: Path, dur: float = XFADE_DUR, style: str = XFADE_STYLE) -> None:
378	    """Replace the hard cut between two already-built segments with a single
379	    merged clip: full seg_a, crossfading (video via xfade, audio in parallel
380	    via acrossfade) into full seg_b over `dur` seconds at the boundary. This
381	    one output clip REPLACES both seg_a and seg_b in the final concat list
382	    (its own duration is dur_a + dur_b - dur, since the overlapping tail/head
383	    now live once, blended, instead of twice). Both segments are already
384	    1920x1080/60fps/libx264/yuv420p/aac from the per-segment build step, so
385	    they're safe to feed straight into xfade/acrossfade as two -i inputs with
386	    no extra normalization needed.
387	
388	    `offset` (xfade's crossfade-start point, measured on seg_a's own
389	    timeline) is computed from seg_a's REAL encoded duration via ffprobe, not
390	    the EDL's nominal (end-start) -- see probe_duration()."""
391	    dur_a = probe_duration(seg_a)
392	    offset = dur_a - dur
393	    if offset < 0:
394	        print(f"FAILED: segment {seg_a} too short ({dur_a}s) for a {dur}s crossfade")
395	        sys.exit(1)
396	    filt = (
397	        f"[0:v][1:v]xfade=transition={style}:duration={dur}:offset={offset}[v];"
398	        f"[0:a][1:a]acrossfade=d={dur}[a]"
399	    )
400	    cmd = [
401	        FFMPEG, "-y",
402	        "-i", str(seg_a), "-i", str(seg_b),
403	        "-filter_complex", filt,
404	        "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]",
405	        "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-c:a", "aac",
406	        str(out), "-loglevel", "error",
407	    ]
408	    run(cmd)

411	def zoom_filter(z: dict) -> str:
412	    # Supersample before zoompan (4x linear) so the crop window's pixel-rounded
413	    # position error shrinks proportionally at output res -- this is what
414	    # actually kills the end-of-ramp "vibration": zoompan rounds x/y to whole
415	    # *input* pixels each frame, and near the top of an ease-out curve many
416	    # consecutive frames have nearly-but-not-quite-identical zoom, so the
417	    # rounded crop position dithers by +/-1px at the sampling resolution.
418	    # At 4x input res, that same 1px dither is a quarter-output-pixel: gone.
419	    # Rounding the zoom value itself to 4 decimals removes the sub-pixel
420	    # floating-point noise that was driving the dither in the first place.
421	    fps = 60
422	    rsf = z["rs"] * fps
423	    rdf = z["rd"] * fps
424	    cx, cy, Z = z["cx"] * 2, z["cy"] * 2, z["z"]  # cx/cy given in 1x source coords; input is prescaled 2x here
425	    in_ease = f"(1-pow(1-min(max((on-{rsf})/{rdf}\\,0)\\,1)\\,3))"
426	    if z.get("out_rs") is not None:
427	        orsf = z["out_rs"] * fps
428	        ordf = z["out_rd"] * fps
429	        out_ease = f"(1-min(max((on-{orsf})/{ordf}\\,0)\\,1))"
430	        raw_zoom = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}*{out_ease}"
431	    else:
432	        raw_zoom = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}"
433	    zoom_expr = f"round(({raw_zoom})*2000)/2000"
434	    x_expr = f"min(max({cx}-(iw/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,iw-iw/zoom)"
435	    y_expr = f"min(max({cy}-(ih/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,ih-ih/zoom)"
436	    zp = f"zoompan=z='{zoom_expr}':x='{x_expr}':y='{y_expr}':d=1:s=1920x1080:fps={fps}"
437	    return f"scale=3840:2160:flags=lanczos,{zp}"

469	def _shrink_u_expr(graphic_start: float, graphic_end: float, td: float) -> str:
470	    """0..1 blend factor for the webcam hero<->corner shrink-aside: 0 = full
471	    hero size/position, 1 = settled corner size/position. Ramps 0->1 (ease-out
472	    cubic) over `td` seconds ending exactly at graphic_start (so the shrink
473	    completes right as the graphic's own CRT entrance begins), holds at 1 for
474	    the graphic's whole window, then ramps back 1->0 over `td` seconds
475	    starting at graphic_end. Same min(ease_in,ease_out) shape as
476	    crt_transition_filter's s_expr, just inverted (0 at the edges instead of
477	    the middle is what we want here since 0 = hero/full-frame, matching s=1
478	    there -- so this reuses s_expr as-is: s=1 in the hold matches u=1 here)."""
479	    ws, we = graphic_start - td, graphic_end + td
480	    p_in = f"min(max((t-{ws})/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
481	    p_out = f"min(max(({we}-t)/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
482	    ease_in = f"(1-pow(1-{p_in}\\,3))"
483	    ease_out = f"(1-pow(1-{p_out}\\,3))"
484	    return f"min({ease_in}\\,{ease_out})"

487	def _hero_transform(idx: int, windows: list[tuple[float, float]], td: float = SHRINK_DUR) -> dict:
488	    """Piecewise scale(w,h)/position(x,y) expressions for the webcam feed,
489	    blending between the hero-stage size/position and this range's
490	    ASIDE_CENTER size/position across one or more graphic windows (see
491	    _shrink_u_expr). Multiple windows combine via max() (they don't overlap
492	    in time)."""
493	    cx, cy = ASIDE_CENTER[idx]
494	    aside_w, aside_h = ASIDE_SIZE[idx]
495	    aside_x, aside_y = cx - aside_w / 2, cy - aside_h / 2
496	    u_terms = [_shrink_u_expr(gs, ge, td) for gs, ge in windows]
497	    u_expr = u_terms[0]
498	    for term in u_terms[1:]:
499	        u_expr = f"max({u_expr}\\,{term})"
500	    w_expr = f"(2*round(({HERO_W}+({aside_w}-{HERO_W})*{u_expr})/2))"
501	    h_expr = f"(2*round(({HERO_H}+({aside_h}-{HERO_H})*{u_expr})/2))"
502	    x_expr = f"({HERO_X}+({aside_x}-{HERO_X})*{u_expr})"
503	    y_expr = f"({HERO_Y}+({aside_y}-{HERO_Y})*{u_expr})"
504	    return dict(w=w_expr, h=h_expr, x=x_expr, y=y_expr, u=u_expr)

511	    """Hero-stage webcam_primary layout: retrowave-loop background, the
512	    webcam feed enlarged to ~980px tall (its native 4:3 aspect preserved,
513	    never distorted) and centered, a neon border loop scaled/recentered to
514	    hug the new larger webcam box, and a subtle full-frame grain/flicker loop
515	    on top of it all. Ranges in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES additionally shrink the
516	    webcam+border ASIDE to that range's ASIDE_CENTER (60-70% of hero size,
517	    moved to whichever side of the screen is clear of that graphic's real
518	    content), eased, while that range's own graphic overlay(s) are on screen
519	    (see OVERLAYS[idx] + _hero_transform), holding there for the graphic's
520	    window before easing back to hero size. The neon border scales/repositions
521	    continuously in lockstep with the webcam throughout (not just at the two
522	    settled endpoints) -- see the border_dyn block below.
523	    The rounded-corner mask (pip_mask.png) is scaled in lockstep with the
524	    webcam feed itself (same w/h expressions) so the corner radius scales
525	    proportionally with the box at every point in the animation, hero size,
526	    corner size, and everywhere in between.
527	
528	    `include_grain` (default True) and `apply_scrim` (default False) are
529	    per-build toggles, not permanent feature removals -- added for the
530	    demo_60s_v2 mockup, which needs grain OFF ("no static", per the user's
531	    latest direction, still going back and forth on it) and a background
532	    scrim ON. `apply_scrim` darkens the RAW retrowave background plate only
533	    (via colorchannelmixer, equivalent to alpha-compositing a flat black
534	    layer at SCRIM_OPACITY opacity: out = src*(1-SCRIM_OPACITY)), same
535	    layering principle as the existing grain fix above -- applied to the
536	    background before the border/webcam/graphic are drawn on top, so it
537	    never darkens the presenter or the graphics, only the plate behind them.
538	    """
539	    dur = end - start
540	    overlays = OVERLAYS.get(idx)
541	    dynamic = idx in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES and overlays
542	
543	    bg_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-i", str(RETROWAVE_BG)]
544	    grain_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(GRAIN_LOOP)]
545	    border_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(NEON_BORDER)]

"""Ken-Burns-style animated push-in zoom for a video segment, via ffmpeg's
zoompan filter. Import zoom_filter_string() from a compositing script, or run
this file directly to print/test one filter string.

WHY THIS EXISTS (hard-won debugging, don't repeat it):

1. ffmpeg's `crop` filter only evaluates its w/h expressions ONCE, at init.
   Only x/y support true per-frame animation. So you CANNOT animate a
   shrinking crop box with `crop=w='...':h='...'` and expect a smooth zoom --
   every frame gets the same (first-computed) w/h, only the position pans.
   `zoompan` is the correct filter for an actual animated zoom level; it has
   no such limitation.

2. zoompan produces a visible "vibration"/jitter right as an ease-out curve
   flattens near its target (many consecutive frames end up with nearly-but-
   not-exactly-identical zoom values, and the resulting crop window's
   pixel-rounded position dithers by +/-1px at the sampling resolution).
   Fix, both required: (a) pre-scale the source 2x before zoompan so that
   same 1px dither becomes a sub-pixel error at output res, and (b) round
   the zoom expression to a fixed precision so floating-point noise near the
   plateau can't produce distinct-but-nearly-equal values frame to frame.

3. When composing the rounding fix as a string template, WRAP THE WHOLE
   INNER EXPRESSION IN PARENTHESES before multiplying: `round((expr)*2000)`,
   not `round(expr*2000)`. ffmpeg's expression parser applies its own
   operator precedence to the resulting string -- multiplication binds
   tighter than the addition inside `expr` (which is `1 + (...)`), so without
   the parens only the last multiplicative term gets scaled, collapsing the
   whole zoom range down near 0 and silently producing NO visible zoom at
   all (still renders successfully, wrong output, easy to ship by accident --
   always pull a before/after frame and confirm the crop actually changed
   size, don't just check the ffmpeg command exits 0).

4. ffmpeg eval expressions have no `clip(x,lo,hi)` function -- use
   `min(max(x,lo),hi)`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations


def zoom_filter_string(
    rs: float,
    rd: float,
    cx: float,
    cy: float,
    zoom: float,
    out_rs: float | None = None,
    out_rd: float | None = None,
    fps: int = 60,
    out_w: int = 1920,
    out_h: int = 1080,
    supersample: int = 2,
) -> str:
    """Build a zoompan-based push-in filter string.

    rs, rd: ramp-in start / duration, in seconds RELATIVE TO THIS SEGMENT'S
        OWN START (i.e. seconds into the extracted clip, not absolute source
        time).
    cx, cy: target crop center, in ORIGINAL (1x, out_w x out_h) source pixel
        coordinates -- e.g. (955, 650) for a point at x=955,y=650 in a
        1920x1080 frame. Internally scaled by `supersample`.
